about: The sound whitelist: every sound a storyboard may name, with what it really sounds like. Hand-edited (make-catalog.mjs copies family/says/scenes into catalog.json). Written from engine/sfx/measure.mjs numbers and the source files, not by ear: Claude can't hear, Jonny's ears decide. A sound that isn't here can't be used, a sound with 'scenes' plays only in a clip that declares one of them ("sound": { "scenes": ["scifi"] }), and 'words' are the names Jonny uses (splort, dö-döm, bonk) that a storyboard may write instead of the id. 'same' = the raw family behind a named sound (use the named one). 'pending' = the sound arrives with an open branch. Search: node engine/sfx/whitelist.mjs wet

families.steps: footsteps, one take per footfall (the auto foley picks the floor from the set)
families.handling: hands and props: grabs, cloth, setting things down, sitting
families.hit: punches, thuds, knocks on wood, metal, glass and plates
families.body: breaths, gasps, heartbeats, mouth sounds, farts
families.cartoon: the engine's cartoon moves: hops, landings, pops, poofs, whooshes, little pings
families.signature: the three leads' fixed signature sounds
families.music: musical stings: a chord, a sad trombone, short jingles
families.street: horns, brakes, air doors, engines, lift doors
families.ui: screen sounds: menu beeps, clicks, swipes, glitches (only in a sci-fi clip or one with a screen)
families.scifi: synth blips, lasers, spaceship engines, sci-fi doors (only in a sci-fi clip or one with a screen)
families.animal: real animal sounds: bear growls, roars, huffs and paws (AI, Stable Audio)
families.weather: thunder, fire, wind and branches: outdoor night ambience and storm sounds (AI, Stable Audio)
families.crash: tearing and smashing: fabric, glass, sheet metal, pots, car alarms (AI, Stable Audio)

scenes.ui: a phone, computer or lift panel on screen whose beeps and swipes we hear
scenes.jingle: the clip plays a musical game-show or video-game sting on purpose

hop.says: a quick little rising blip, 0.13 s (a cartoon jump)

land.says: a short low thump that drops in pitch (feet landing)

whoosh.says: air rushing past: a band of noise that swells and fades, about 0.3 s

charge.says: a rising electric whine with sparkles getting denser, 1.3 s (a spell charging up), sometimes a little chime on top

impact.says: a big deep boom that drops in pitch, with a metallic ring on top (a heavy cartoon hit)

poof.says: a soft puff of air going darker, about 0.9 s (a cloud of smoke); about half the time a little magic chime on top

pop.says: a bubble pop: a quick upward blip and a short ringing tone at 1.4 kHz

timestop.says: time stopping: a dry wooden clock TOCK with a click on top (loudest at 0.01 s), under it a low buzzy tone sliding down from about 380 to 60 Hz over 0.8 s like a tape stopping, a falling band of air, and a faint clock-bell ring (1.6 kHz) dying away, 1.3 s (code-made; the what-if pause's power sound)

timego.says: time starting again: a quick rising 'vwip' gliding from about 70 Hz up to 700 Hz in 0.22 s, ending in one bright clock tick (2.4 kHz), 0.42 s (code-made)

timer-beep.says: one short pure beep, steady at about 3 kHz, 0.08 s (a camera's self-timer counting down; code-made)

bubbling.says: a low wet bubbling bed with about 17 small pops a second on top (around 350-430 Hz, dark), fading in and out; length = its dur (hot oil boiling in a giant fryer; code-made)

rumble.says: a low dark rumble, almost all under 200 Hz (around 80 Hz), swelling slowly to its end; length = its dur (a furnace far off; code-made)

steam.says: a hard bright hiss (centroid about 11 kHz) that bursts in at once and tails off, 0.7 s by default (a fierce steam jet from a pipe; code-made)

ridewind.says: a dark gusty roar of rushing air (centroid about 640 Hz, a third of it under 200 Hz) swelling and easing a few times a second; length = its dur (riding fast, wind past the ears; code-made)

windswell.says: the same dark roar of air (centroid about 750 Hz) rising from quiet to loud over its length, loudest near the end; 1.2 s by default (the wind rising as the ground drops away; code-made)

tyres.says: a low buzzing rumble (a band around 240 Hz, fluttering) with fine bright gravel ticks on top, about 14 a second; length = its dur (bicycle tyres on a dirt trail; code-made)

freewheel.says: soft even metallic ticks, about 11 a second, each a short bright ping near 2.9 kHz; length = its dur (a bicycle's freewheel and chain while pedalling gently; code-made)

plank-rattle.says: a hollow dark wooden rumble with quick uneven knocks (around 200-250 Hz, about 9 a second), 0.7 s by default (bicycle wheels rolling over a wooden plank; code-made)

dinostomp.says: a giant's footfall: a deep thump gliding down 48->39 Hz with a dull mid knock on top (centroid about 730 Hz, so a phone hears it), loudest at once, a little grit trickling after, 0.9 s (a T-rex stepping; code-made)

snort.says: a big animal sniffing: a sharp nasal intake, airy noise rising through a band from about 600 to 1400 Hz with a small flutter, loudest past the middle, 0.3 s (a T-rex sniffing; code-made)

dinoroar.says: a cartoon dinosaur roar, more trumpet than horror: a brassy buzzing bray (sawtooth round 215 Hz, centroid about 780 Hz, nothing under 300 Hz) that swells, wobbles and sags in pitch, with breathy noise under it, 1.2 s (code-made)

waves.says: small waves lapping on a shallow beach: soft surges of washy noise round 700 Hz every 2.6 s with a bright fizz as each one breaks, nothing under 200 Hz, a bed of any length (code-made)

whistletune.says: someone whistling an innocent little tune through the lips: a pure breathy tone round 1.1-1.3 kHz, nine short notes in two sing-song bars with a held note at the end, 1.7 s (code-made)

whistle.says: a lifeguard's pea whistle: a bright trilling tone steady round 2.9 kHz, two short blasts and a long one, 0.9 s (code-made)

feedback.says: a megaphone's feedback squeal: a piercing buzzy tone gliding up from about 1.9 to 2.8 kHz as it swells, 0.7 s (code-made)

ringpop.says: an inflatable ring bursting: a sharp bang of bright noise round 1.8 kHz, loudest in the first 10 ms, with a thin rubber slap at 520 Hz, 0.13 s (code-made)

deflate.says: air rushing out of a popped ring: a long fluttering pfffrrt of hissy noise sagging from about 1.4 kHz to 800 Hz, loudest at the start, 1.4 s (code-made)

sharkhum.says: a plush shark's hopeful little hum with its mouth shut: two soft warm "mm-mm?" notes, the second gliding up like a question (about 310 to 450 Hz with harmonics), 0.7 s (code-made)

groan.says: a tired cartoon zombie's groan: a low nasal buzzy uhhhh round 150 Hz with a vowel band near 700 Hz, sagging and wobbling; a long one is three overlapping voices (a horde), never scary (code-made)

leafrustle.says: leaves rustling as someone dives into a hedge: a dense crackle of small dry clicks in airy noise above 1.8 kHz that swells and settles, 0.6 s (code-made)

pat.says: a soft friendly pat on a shoulder: a muffled cloth slap, a short thump round 300 Hz with a little noise up to 2 kHz, 0.12 s (code-made)

lampbuzz.says: an old street lamp buzzing: a mains hum at 120 Hz with bright odd harmonics up to about 1.5 kHz, stuttering as the lamp flickers; a bed of any length (code-made)

flamejet.says: a roaring fwoosh of flame: a dark rushing roar (centroid about 2.4 kHz, a low body gliding 350->280 Hz) with a fluttering edge and a few crackles, bursts in, loudest at 0.3 s, tails off by 0.8 s (a jet of fire from a pipe; code-made)

gulp.says: one cartoon swallow, 'glk': a tiny click, then a short low bloop that rises and falls round 200-350 Hz, 0.19 s, two hits (a mouthful going down; code-made)

crumble.says: a plaster wall breaking: a dry crack and a low crunchy burst (loudest at once), then about ten small pieces clattering down over 0.9 s (centroid about 1.3 kHz; code-made)

sizzle.says: a quiet bright airy hiss with about nine tiny crackles in it, 0.8 s (cloth starting to smoulder; code-made)

flash.says: a camera firing: a sharp click, a short bright 'pff' of noise and a second click, 0.23 s (code-made)

click.says: two tiny sharp clicks (a camera shutter or a light switch)

creak.says: a slow rough squeak wobbling around 650 Hz (a lid straining, a hinge)

shing.says: a bright metal ring that rises a little (a blade drawn, a sword gleam)

knock-tap.says: one hollow knuckle-on-door thud with a click on top (the engine's own knock; 'knock' is the AI one Jonny picked)

slam.says: a deep door thump, the frame rattling and a latch click (code-made)

tink.says: a tiny high metal ping, 0.35 s (a coin, a hat brim tapping something)

ting.says: a high bright bell ping that rings out, 0.7 s (light glinting off a blade): this is a 'bling'

crinkle.says: a few quick crisp crackles (a sweet wrapper)

latch.says: an iron latch dropping into its catch: a metal clack with a short ring (code-made)

patter.says: popcorn raining down: dozens of tiny dry ticks (centroid about 4.2 kHz, no bass), thick at first and thinning out over about 1 s, a few softer papery taps under them (code-made, Too Much Energy 02)

seatclack.says: a cinema seat cushion springing up or slammed down: a short hollow woody clack round 650 Hz (centroid about 0.9 kHz, 0.17 s) with a small padded thump and a tiny hinge tick (code-made, Too Much Energy 02)

zip.says: a tent door zip pulled fast: a bright noisy rasp of zip-teeth clicks (centroid about 4.2 kHz, no bass) whose rate climbs as the pull speeds up, about 0.2 s long by default (follows dur), a tiny tick at the end (code-made, Too Much Energy 03)

scarestab.says: a horror film's jump-scare hit: a dissonant cluster of buzzy saw tones (about 325 Hz, centroid 0.54 kHz) over a small low boom, full at once and dying over 1.1 s (code-made, Too Much Energy 02)

brassswell.says: a brass swell for a film hero winning: an E major chord of warm saw tones that grows and brightens over its first half, loudest at about 0.67 s, then holds to its end (default 1 s; code-made, Too Much Energy 02)

papercut.says: a dry tearing hiss with a soft thock (a blade through paper or card)

rocket.says: a firework rocket climbing: a whistle gliding up from about 920 Hz to 2.2 kHz over a fizzing spray of bright crackles, swelling to its loudest at the very end and stopping dead, 1 s (code-made)

thunder.says: thunder close by: a hard dry crack on its first frame, then a boom that rolls away in about five uneven swells, 2.8 s by default (code-made; the crack and a band round 320 Hz carry it on a phone)

firework.says: a firework shell bursting: loudest on its first frame, a sharp crack and a punchy mid thump over a deep boom sinking 54->48 Hz, then a crackling shimmer of tiny ticks thinning out, 1.8 s (code-made; 69 % of its energy is under 200 Hz, the crack and thump carry it on a phone)

explosion.says: a big fuel explosion close by: loudest on its first frame, a short crack, a fireball roar that sinks in pitch, a deep boom sinking 62->34 Hz, a second smaller blast after 0.4 s, then debris ticks over a tail of burning, 3 s by default (code-made; bands round 380 and 900 Hz carry it on a phone)

fizzle.says: a small weak firework far off: a dull little pff (noise round 900 Hz) on its first frame and a thin bright sputter that dies within half a second (code-made)

blow.says: a breath blown through pursed lips: an airy fff, noise around 1.4 kHz with a little flutter, about 0.7 s (blowing at a candle), from its code

plunk.says: one dry muted low pluck, 'dum' (A2, 110 Hz), gone by 0.3 s with no tail (a deadpan button), from its code

gasp.says: a quick breathy inhale that rises (a small surprised gasp)

step.says: one heavy footstep on stone: a dull low thud and a little grit (code-made)

sting.says: one dark minor chord of buzzy saw tones, 0.7 s: a single 'dun!' (a shock). Off by default on a shocked face: "sound": { "autoSting": true }

screech.says: a narrow hissing squeal sliding down (brakes)

ring.says: an alarm clock: a hammer trilling fast between two high bells

alarmbell.says: a bank's alarm bell ringing without a gap: a metal bell struck 22 times a second, each strike a bright clang (body 760 Hz, partials near 1.9, 2.9, 4.3 and 5.6 kHz, about 40 ms decay), a steady hard ring, centroid about 1.8 kHz; 2 s by default, whole strikes so it loops back to back (code-made)

siren.says: a police 'whoop': a near-sine tone with two odd harmonics sweeping 550 to 1450 Hz over 70 % of its length, then falling back to 700 Hz, a little grit; 1.2 s by default, repeats the whoop once per 1.2 s from 2.4 s on; loud and steady (code-made)

sirenwail.says: a police siren far away, the slow two-tone wail: a tone swinging between 650 and 950 Hz, 0.9 s a cycle, low-passed at 1.8 kHz, 12 dB under siren (a bed under a voice); 4 s by default (code-made)

chopper.says: a helicopter overhead: a rotor thump 11 a second (dark noise bursts round 90 Hz with a slap at 900 Hz) over a faint turbine whine near 1.6 kHz, swelling in over 0.5 s and out over 0.5 s; 3 s by default (code-made)

gull.says: a seagull's cry, 'kee-yah, yah, yah': three falling squawks (0.22, 0.18, 0.18 s), each a nasal tone gliding from 2.6 to 1.6 kHz with a fast vibrato; 0.9 s (code-made)

radio.says: a police radio keying: a 30 ms squelch click, band-passed static (700 Hz to 3 kHz) for the middle and a short 1.2 kHz roger beep (80 ms) at the end; 0.5 s by default (code-made)

netshot.says: a net launcher: a dull compressed-air 'pfft' (a 15 ms thump at 140 Hz, then noise sweeping from 6 kHz down to 900 Hz over 0.2 s), then a thin rope whistle rising to 2.5 kHz and fading; 0.6 s by default (code-made)

cuffs.says: handcuffs closing: five quick ratchet clicks 45 ms apart, each a little higher (2.3 to 3 kHz), then one firmer metal clack (2.2 and 5.1 kHz, about 60 ms decay); 0.45 s (code-made)

scribble.says: a pencil writing fast: short scratchy strokes

bell.says: a school bell: a fast hammer on one big bell, about 1 s

splash.says: a puddle splash: a burst of noise and two falling bloops, 0.5 s

ding.says: one soft bell tone at 1.2 kHz that rings out for 1.6 s (a lift arriving)

doorslide.says: sliding doors gliding: a soft low rumble and a whisper of air (lift doors, automatic shop doors)

hiss.says: a short bright hiss of air (bus doors, air brakes)

partyhorn.says: a buzzy paper party horn that bends up as it unrolls

ringtone.says: a phone ringing: a fast trill of two tones in short bursts

flutter.says: a flurry of paper: many soft flaps thinning out

scrape.says: wooden stool feet dragged over a wooden floor: a woody, chattering rub

wings.says: soft feathery wing beats three times a second, for a hover (a bed; the auto wing flaps replace it where they play)

notify.says: a soft phone notification: two quick rounded tones going up a fourth

gunshot.says: a cartoon pistol: a sharp crack and a short low boom

sadslide.says: the sad trombone: four notes sliding down, 'wah wah wah-wahhh', 1.8 s. Off by default on a droop: "sound": { "autoTrombone": true }

puncture.says: a tiny dry card pop with a soft thock (a fang or straw through a carton), from its code

squirt.says: a wet, hissy jet whose pitch drops as the pressure goes, with bubbly flutter (a squeezed carton), from its code

slap.says: a sharp mid-bright crack (centroid about 2.9 kHz) with a short woody knock under it, 0.24 s, little bass (a flat hand slapping a banknote down on a wooden counter; code-made)

recordscratch.says: a vinyl record scratch: a buzzy rubbing tone dragged back and forth, four quick rubs gliding about 510-840 Hz, 0.45 s (the music stopping dead; code-made)

splort.says: a soft wet slap, a squelch sinking in pitch, then a few drips (juice landing on a face), from its code

sig-phoenix.says: Phoenix's flame whoosh: air rushing in, a low 'fwoomp' and roar, embers crackling, a short bird cry, 1.3 s

sig-reaper.says: Reaper's bell: one deep church-bell toll in D that slowly swells and fades, 2.8 s

sig-wizard.says: the Wizard's sparkle: eight quick bell-like notes running up, a high twinkle and glitter, 1.4 s (heard as a 'bling')
